writeup: TIC 43791794 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 0.05%, repeating every 16.2672 days, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal achieves a detection significance of 23.8 in the box-least-squares search, and pixel-level image analysis confirms a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 27.7, with a centroid offset of 17.3 arcsec from the target position. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be a previously unknown system. The machine-learning screening model assigned it a score of 0.91, indicating high confidence that this represents a genuine stellar target. The candidate passed all data quality checks without any outstanding concerns.
